title: Draymond Green Returns to Warriors on One-Year, $27.7 Million Deal
dek: Draymond Green agreed to a one-year, $27.7 million deal with the Golden State Warriors after declining his $27.6 million player option. The deal lacks a no-trade clause. Green's re-signing comes after the Warriors stepped away from trade talks with Milwaukee and after LeBron James chose to sign with Philadelphia.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: Green chose a new one-year deal with the Warriors over his existing $27.6M option, stabilizing the roster after months of trade uncertainty involving the Bucks.
bottom_line: Green's return on a one-year deal keeps the Warriors' core intact as they reset after the failed LeBron pursuit, but the lack of trade protection underscores that the franchise retains flexibility if roster changes become necessary. The market will watch whether the Warriors use this season to build toward another championship window or pivot to younger rotational pieces.
body: Draymond Green agreed to a one-year, $27.7 million contract to remain with the Golden State Warriors, according to ESPN. Klutch Sports CEO Rich Paul, Green's representative, informed ESPN's Shams Charania of the agreement.

Green's deal marks a shift after he declined his $27.6 million player option earlier in the offseason, creating financial flexibility for the Warriors as they pursued free agents during the opening weeks of the summer market. Golden State was among the teams positioned to sign free agent forward LeBron James. After James decided to join the Philadelphia 76ers, the Warriors and Green moved forward on a new agreement.

The new one-year deal does not include a no-trade clause, per ESPN, leaving Green exposed to potential roster moves despite the fresh commitment. That absence of protection stands in contrast to the significant role Green has held in the franchise's core.

Green's tenure with the Warriors now spans 14 seasons. According to ESPN, that 14-season run is the second-longest active streak for a player with one team in the NBA, behind only his teammate Stephen Curry, who will begin his 18th season with Golden State in October.

The past season featured considerable uncertainty for Green. In February, league sources told ESPN that Green was part of the Warriors' trade discussions with the Milwaukee Bucks centered on acquiring superstar Giannis Antetokounmpo. Green acknowledged the unease that period generated. "I'm a human being. There was a second of me [at the deadline] that felt like, 'Damn, they really going to do that to me?'" Green told ESPN in March, per the reporting. "But I understand this business probably [as] good as any player. Like, yo, this is Giannis Antetokounmpo. They not just about to trade me for a bag of peanuts." The Warriors did not pursue that trade further and declined to reenter talks with Milwaukee this summer.
Green averaged 27.5 minutes in 68 games last season. He has indicated willingness to move into a bench role if head coach Steve Kerr determines that is the best fit for the roster.
